label: Arrived at City College of New York
description: Davis began his undergraduate studies as a freshman.

sources.quote: He arrived at City College of New York as a freshman in 1944 and soon became interested in the foundations of real analysis and in logic.

label: Received PhD from Princeton University
description: Davis completed his PhD under the guidance of Church.

sources.quote: he got his PhD in just two years, under the guidance of Church, in 1950.

label: Recruited to Control Systems Laboratory
description: Davis began programming computers for an ORDVAC machine.

sources.quote: Martin began to program computers in 1951, when he was recruited to a group that developed programs for an ORDVAC machine, in support of the military during the Korean War.

label: Implemented Presburger's algorithm on JOHNNIAC
description: Davis implemented the algorithm at the Institute for Advanced Study.

sources.quote: Martin's implementation of that algorithm took place on a JOHNNIAC computer available at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton in the summer of 1954.

label: Discovered Davis-Putnam-Robinson theorem
description: Davis and Putnam hit the jackpot on the original discovery.

sources.quote: "It was in the summer of 1959 that Hilary and I really hit the jackpot," he says, to describe the original, raw discovery of what would become known as the celebrated Davis–Putnam–Robinson theorem).

label: Published DPLL procedure paper
description: Davis and colleagues published the machine program for theorem-proving.

sources.quote: The Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland procedure [11] (DPLL for short), still fundamental in today's architectures of fast Boolean satisfiability solvers, was rooted in that collaboration.

label: Learned of Matiyasevich's work
description: Davis learned of the work that completed the proof of H10.

sources.quote: "One of the great pleasures of my life came in February 1970, when I learned of the work of Yuri Matiyasevich which completed the proof of the crucial conjecture and thereby showed that Hilbert's Tenth Problem is recursively unsolvable."

label: Taught summer course in Perugia
description: Davis offered a course on computability in Italy.

sources.quote: In 1975, Martin offered a summer course on computability in the pretty Italian town of Perugia.

label: Phone call with Shlapentokh
description: Davis encouraged Shlapentokh to come to NYU.

sources.quote: I first spoke to Martin (on the phone) in the Spring of 1983 when I was deciding on a graduate school.

label: Hosted party for two Yuri's
description: Davis hosted Matiyasevich and Gurevich in New York.

sources.quote: On the evening of a beautiful day of the fall of 1990, I was invited by Martin to his place in the Upper West Side in New York, to a "party for two Yuri's."

label: Visited George Washington University
description: Davis gave a math colloquium talk.

sources.quote: It was in November 2007 and his lecture was entitled "Unsolvability and undecidability in the Diophantine realm,"

label: Gave MSRI talk
description: Davis gave an opening talk for the MSRI semester program.

sources.quote: Martin Davis's 2020 talk, "Here there be monsters," was possible when MSRI semester program on Decidability, Definability and Computability in Number Theory had to be moved online.
